nodes.name: Robust and efficient visual odometry using colored point cloud maps via dual-sparsity and hierarchical optimization
nodes.venue: Satellite Navigation
nodes.abstract: Abstract Reliable localization is fundamental to navigation in GNSS-challenged environments, yet monocular visual odometry (VO) inevitably suffers from drift without global constraints. Point cloud maps can provide global corrections to mitigate this drift. However, existing heterogeneous feature registration methods fail to fully exploit the shared information between vision and point clouds. This limitation results in suboptimal localization accuracy, reduced robustness, and increased computational overhead. To address these issues, we propose a visual odometry system based on colored point cloud maps, which leverages both the global point cloud map as a constraint and the shared modality (color) between the colored point cloud map and the camera to ensure localization accuracy and robustness. The system consists of two main components: sparse colored point cloud construction and visual localization. In the sparse colored point cloud construction module, we introduce a map sparsification strategy that associates visual gradients with point clouds, ensuring that the retained sparse point cloud preserves salient visual gradient information, thereby reducing computational costs. This strategy is further incorporated into the vision-to-map matching stage, forming a “dual-sparsity matching” scheme. In the localization stage, we propose a hierarchical optimization-based iterative Kalman filtering algorithm, which performs multi-level iterative optimization over multi-resolution images to prevent localization from getting trapped in local optima while enhancing accuracy. Experiments on public and self-collected sequences demonstrate significant gains in both accuracy and efficiency. Compared with a representative map-based method (DSL), the proposed approach reduces ATE (RMSE) by $$52\%$$ 52 % – $$95\%$$ 95 % across multiple challenging sequences, with a representative improvement from 1.883 to $$0.152\,\text {m}$$ 0.152 m on R3live_5 ( $$91.92\%$$ 91.92 % reduction). Against the learning-based I2D-Loc++, our method achieves accuracy gains of up to $$76.6\%$$ 76.6 % and maintains robust tracking in extreme cases (e.g., R3live_3/4 ) where I2D-Loc++ and ORB-SLAM3 fail due to visual degradation. Furthermore, the system maintains near real-time efficiency, reducing total processing time by up to $$47.7\%$$ 47.7 % (e.g., from 121.11 to $$63.34\,\text {s}$$ 63.34 s on Whu_1 ). Even under severe geometric degeneracy, our tracker remains robust with an ATE of $$0.076\,\text {m}$$ 0.076 m , whereas geometry-only LiDAR–IMU localization degrades to $$9.23\,\text {m}$$ 9.23 m .

nodes.name: Enhancing sparse multi-view super-resolution with unified multi-plane image spatial representation
nodes.venue: Visual Intelligence
nodes.abstract: Abstract The popularization of multi-camera systems and multi-view image capture has led to the emergence of sparse multi-view image super-resolution (MVSR) as a promising research direction. The primary approach to sparse multi-view super-resolution (SR) currently involves extending traditional single-view SR and stereo SR frameworks, i.e., extracting features from each view and performing pixel-domain alignment and fusion to leverage cross-view reference information. However, this straightforward framework has two main drawbacks. First, performing cross-view fusion in the pixel domain disregards the spatial perception information that multi-view images provide. Second, feature alignment and fusion across views introduce considerable redundant and repetitive computations, which hinders further scalability to more viewpoints. This paper proposes a novel sparse multi-view SR framework based on a unified spatial representation reference. Specifically, the proposed method first computes a multi-plane image spatial representation from the multi-view images. This multi-plane image (MPI) representation encapsulates all the information from each view and has spatial perception. Subsequently, an upsampled reference image is rendered from the MPI representation for the low-resolution views. A high-low frequency separation fusion network is then proposed to upscale the input low-resolution images based on the rendered reference. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for recovering high-frequency details.

nodes.name: Pareto-based parameter screening for mid- and high-spatial-frequency errors in CO <sub>2</sub> laser beam figuring of fused silica
nodes.venue: Applied Optics
nodes.abstract: Laser beam figuring (LBF) with microsecond-pulsed CO 2 laser radiation enables nanometer-precision material removal on fused silica for deterministic surface figure correction in high-performance optical fabrication. This work presents a framework combining experimentally measured single-pulse craters with a geometric line-synthesis model to construct geometric reference topographies under a pulse-independent-kernel assumption as a function of pulse duration t p and pulse spacing d x . A Pareto-dominance analysis of 60 parameter combinations quantifies the trade-off between mid-spatial-frequency (MSFE) and high-spatial-frequency (HSFE) roughness over a bounded synthesis window, where it arises from the line terminations. Within the investigated parameter space, equal weighting selects t p =90µs and d x =5−10µm for a single pass ( R q MSFE =6.17−6.40nm, R q HSFE =1.06−1.34nm). A limited experimental comparison at two pulse spacings shows substantial deviations from the geometric reference model at high overlap. At equal weighting, the measured lines favor the larger of the two pitches. A transient thermal simulation indicates interpulse heat accumulation. The reported optimum is therefore a property of the defined synthesis construction rather than a validated prediction of fabricated surfaces.

nodes.name: Self‐Powered Photodetection and Optical Information Recognition in a Mixed‐Dimensional WSe <sub>2</sub> /CdSe Heterojunction
nodes.venue: Nanophotonics
nodes.abstract: ABSTRACT Mixed‐dimensional van der Waals heterojunctions offer opportunities for self‐powered optical sensing and information processing, yet identifying the spatial origin of zero‐bias photoresponse remains important for understanding device operation. Here, a vertical WSe 2 /CdSe heterojunction composed of a WSe 2 nanosheet and a CdSe nanobelt is investigated for visible photodetection. Under 610 nm illumination, the device exhibits a photovoltaic response with an open‐circuit voltage of 0.403 V and a short‐circuit current of 4.77 × 10 −10 A. Quantitative photocurrent mapping reveals a mean response of 5.94 nA in the heterojunction overlap region, approximately 50 times that near the metal contacts. Scanning Kelvin probe microscopy yields a reproducible contact‐potential‐difference contrast of 293 ± 15 mV, whereas electronic‐structure calculations support a type‐II band‐edge configuration and interfacial charge redistribution. At 100 Hz, the measured rise/fall times are 1.09/0.99 ms at 0 V and 165/191 μs at +3 V. Under +3 V bias, approximately 97% of the reference modulation amplitude is retained at 1 kHz. Self‐powered optical imaging and wavelength‐ and time‐window‐dependent 8‐bit information recognition are further demonstrated, with all 96 tested bits correctly decoded. These results highlight the potential of mixed‐dimensional WSe 2 /CdSe heterojunctions for self‐powered visible‐light sensing and optical information recognition.

nodes.name: Uncertainty-aware XCO <sub>2</sub> mapping over China through adaptive fusion of multi-source satellite observations
nodes.abstract: Abstract. Multi-source satellite observations of the column-averaged dry-air mole fraction of carbon dioxide (XCO2) are limited by sparse orbital sampling, cross-platform footprint mismatch, and heterogeneous retrieval uncertainties, leading to substantial spatial discontinuities and uncertainty propagation errors in regional XCO2 mapping. To address these limitations, we developed an adaptive fusion framework integrating physics-based Gaussian oversampling and Bayesian maximum entropy (PGO-BME) for uncertainty-aware monthly XCO2 reconstruction over China. Monthly observations from DQ-1, OCO-2, OCO-3, and GOSAT collected between June 2022 and December 2024 were fused within the framework. In hold-out validation, the framework achieved an overall R2 of 0.90 and an RMSE of 0.63 ppm, substantially outperforming conventional pixel-center and area-weighting approaches. Independent validation against the Total Carbon Column Observing Network (TCCON) further showed R2 values of 0.93 at both the Hefei and Xianghe stations. The reconstructed dataset preserved both large-scale atmospheric transport patterns and localized anthropogenic enhancements, while posterior uncertainties were consistent with the corresponding spatial prediction errors. These results demonstrate that physically constrained, uncertainty-aware fusion can improve the spatial continuity and reliability of satellite XCO2 fields while retaining atmospheric CO2 variability across spatial scales.

nodes.name: SynForge-Cardio: a unified multimodal synthetic dataset generation framework for privacy-preserving cardiovascular AI
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Digital Health
nodes.abstract: Multimodal cardiovascular AI systems benefit from jointly available chest radiographs, 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs), and structured electronic health record (EHR) variables. In practice, multi-institutional model development is constrained by privacy regulations, institutional data silos, and class imbalance for less common findings. Existing open-source synthetic data tools are largely modality-specific: tabular libraries such as Synthetic Data Vault (SDV)/Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN), image generators based on latent diffusion, and time-series methods such as Time-series Generative Adversarial Network (TimeGAN) each require its own setup, configuration, and validation. This study presents SynForge-Cardio, a multimodality orchestration framework for prompt-driven synthetic dataset generation across chest X-ray (CXR), 12-lead ECG, and EHR modalities. Rather than introducing a new generative backbone, SynForge-Cardio coordinates established components—latent diffusion with optional low-rank adaptation for CXR; parametric and bounded morphology-preserving augmentation (with an optional TimeGAN path) for ECG; and size-aware routing among jitter augmentation, Gaussian copula, and CTGAN/Tabular Variational Autoencoder for EHR—behind a shared clinical prompt interface, a rule-based router, and a postgeneration quality/privacy reporting layer. The three modalities were generated independently from separate datasets; the framework does not perform patient-level joint synthesis and makes no claim of anatomical or physiological consistency across modalities. This system is implemented as a FastAPI backend with a React frontend and can run on a single workstation GPU. Herein, we formalize the orchestration objective, specify modality-wise models and metrics [Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), dynamic time warping (DTW), power spectral density similarity, Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistics, correlation preservation, and distance-to-closest-record privacy screening], and describe an evaluation protocol on public corpora (NIH Chest X-ray14, PTB-XL, and the UCI Cleveland Heart Disease dataset), including a four-regime train-on-synthetic/test-on-real (TSTR) utility analysis with five random seeds. On the framework alone, we measured 94.6% modality-routing accuracy, 100% direct-vs.-routed generation equivalence on the evaluated cases, 59 unnecessary generator calls avoided, and 100% validation/reporting completeness (1,105/1,108 tests pass, 3 skipped). Downstream-utility results were mixed: augmenting a 25%-real training set with synthetic data changed the held-out AUROC by −0.041 to +0.050 across three CXR tasks (none significant at five seeds); by +0.019 for ECG MI-vs.-NORM [produced by mode B (bounded real-waveform augmentation, whose synthetic samples can be matched to their true source recording at top-1 ≈ 42.7–43.4%, and hence, mode B is not an independently learned generative model)]; and by +0.017 for EHR heart disease classification, which is not evidence of benefit given the 61-record hold-out set (the test-set bootstrap 95% CI for the difference includes zero). Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV acquisition was not completed because credentialed access was unavailable; all reported EHR results were UCI-based. SynForge-Cardio is intended as a practical, reproducible research framework for privacy-conscious cardiovascular data augmentation and prototype development.

nodes.name: Subpixel Low-Intensity Fire Detection in Wide-Swath Remote Sensing: Dual-Scale Thermal Background Adaptation and Spatiotemporal Semantic Constraints
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Subpixel low-intensity fires are difficult to detect in wide-swath imagery because mixed pixels weaken their thermal signals, whereas industrial facilities and photovoltaic panels can generate false alarms. We propose a dual-scale adaptive thermal background thresholding method based on spatiotemporal semantic constraints and conduct experiments using the detection of crop straw burning in China as a specific application scenario. The method combines scene-wide thermal state classification with local neighborhood statistics to adjust the above-background threshold and recover additional weak fire candidates. Farmland support, a persistent heat source prior derived from long-term VIIRS observations, and candidate-to-source proximity are then applied to newly added candidates to suppress non-target anomalies while preserving strong thermal detections. Experiments using 36 Wide Swath Imager scenes, near-contemporaneous Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite observations, field surveys in Anhui Province, and 260 Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer scenes support the method’s use for weak fire candidate screening under heterogeneous thermal backgrounds. Targeted field surveys found fresh crop residue burn marks at 10 of 12 selected T0 candidate sites (83.3%). This proportion applies only to the surveyed candidate set and does not represent an estimate of overall detection accuracy. In the MODIS transfer experiment, detections near industrial facilities decreased from 45.17% for the official products to 7.92% with the transferred method. The proposed framework supports the regional screening of low-intensity fire candidates and targeted field verification, with persistent heat source information providing contextual constraints.

nodes.name: Spatial or Common Correlated Effects? A Sequential Pretest and the Risk of the Post-Test Estimator
nodes.venue: Econometrics
nodes.abstract: Macroeconomic panels display two forms of cross-sectional dependence usually treated as rival specifications: unobserved common factors with heterogeneous loadings, which motivate common correlated effects estimators, and spatial spillovers, which motivate spatial autoregressive models. This article specifies and evaluates a sequential pretest: common factors are filtered through cross-sectional averages, the residuals are tested for spatial dependence with Moran’s I, and the estimator is chosen accordingly. A Monte Carlo experiment with 96 cells and 1000 replications each varies the weight matrix, spatial parameter, number of factors and panel dimensions. The annual Moran test on filtered residuals is correctly sized, but a rule requiring rejection in a quarter of the periods is conservative by construction. Detection does not translate into lower risk: with common factors and moderate spatial dependence, a more powerful rule raises the mean squared error of the post-test estimator, even when calibrated by permutation, while a joint spatial–factor estimator keeps a low risk and close to nominal coverage if the weight matrix is correctly specified. Applied to 18 Latin American economies (2000–2021), the pretest selects the factor-based estimator and the mean group joint estimator, unlike the pooled one, finds no significant spatial lag.

nodes.name: Spatial Attention Mechanism for Improved Multi-Focus Satellite Image Fusion: SARA-Net Model
nodes.venue: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology
nodes.abstract: Multi-focus image fusion is crucial in various fields, particularly in satellite images, because it creates intricate images with augmented clarity. However, maintaining the original structure is challenging, leading to a reduction in performance. Therefore, this research proposes a Spatial Attention ResNet-50 Network (SARA-Net) model for fusing multiple satellite images. The proposed model utilizes an integration of ResNet-50 and Spatial Attention to effectively extract spatially significant features from actual images. Initially, satellite images from the publicly available SpaceNet datasets are preprocessed by normalization and grayscale conversion to provide consistency. ResNet-50 handles multi-scale feature extraction by residual learning, which addresses vanishing gradient issues, whereas spatial attention assigns adaptive weights to improve relevant spatial information within the feature map. The fusion layer combines these attention features to generate high-resolution and detail-preserving images. On the ten held-out test images, the proposed SARA-Net achieves a PSNR of 48.972 dB, an SSIM of 0.9953, and an entropy value of 8.4319, which is better than the existing methods.

nodes.name: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology
SMNDO-PWD: A Density-Adaptive Otsu Framework for Cross-Regional Detection of Pine Wilt Disease Using RGB Imagery and Spectral Reconstruction
nodes.venue: Forests
nodes.abstract: Pine wilt disease (PWD) has caused extensive damage to pine forests in China. However, large-scale monitoring using high-resolution imagery is constrained by the high cost of hyperspectral data and the annotation requirements of task-specific deep learning models. To address these challenges, this study proposes SMNDO-PWD, a remote sensing framework for detecting PWD-affected trees. First, a pretrained SegFormer (MiT-B5) model removes non-vegetation features such as buildings and bare soil. MST++ then reconstructs statistically plausible hyperspectral bands in the 400–700 nm range from the RGB imagery, and the normalized difference index (NDI) is computed from the reconstructed 670 nm and 550 nm bands. Subsequently, support vector machine (SVM)-based density classification is integrated with density-adaptive dynamic Otsu thresholding to extract PWD-affected trees, requiring only lightweight classifier training and threshold optimization. Results from three reference plots in Shaoguan show that SMNDO-PWD achieves average pixel-level intersection over union (IoU) and F1 scores 51.28% and 32.14% higher, respectively, than YOLOv8s-seg. Further evaluation across eight cities in six provinces yields average IoU and F1 scores of 0.52 and 0.69, respectively, using manual annotations as reference. Ablation experiments confirm the contributions and complementary effects of individual modules. Furthermore, an application covering approximately 900 ha in Zhaoqing demonstrates the potential of SMNDO-PWD for large-scale monitoring. The framework also enables the quantification of the affected area ratio (AAR), affected area, and the relative NDI distribution in the affected areas, providing spatial information to support PWD assessment and management.

nodes.name: Remote Sensing and GIS Integration for Spatiotemporal Assessment of Environmental Deterioration and Pollution to Support Coastal Lakes Sustainability
nodes.venue: Sustainability
nodes.abstract: Coastal lakes in the Mediterranean are highly sensitive ecosystems facing increasing pressure from the combined effects of anthropogenic activities and climate change. This study examined environmental changes in five Egyptian Mediterranean coastal lakes: Mariout, Edku, Burullus, Manzala, and Bardawil from 2020 to 2025, including an intermediate dataset for 2022. The assessment combined the Integrated Water Quality Index (IWQI), a Relative TDS Proxy (rTDS), and aquatic surface-cover classification derived from Sentinel-2 MSI imagery. All indicators were standardized using Z-score normalization and integrated using a weighted framework. Here, lake classifications are based solely on their connectivity to the Mediterranean Sea, regardless of other inland water sources. In Mariout (fully closed to the sea), continuous wastewater input drove a 4 km2 contraction and severe homogenization. Edku (partially open) showed a “phantom recovery” of open water (+20.84 km2) masking a 24.74% vegetation collapse and rTDS polarization. Burullus (partially open) remained relatively stable, though an 8.66 km2/yr vegetation expansion suggests a stagnation-feedback loop. Manzala (restricted-exchange) showed extreme aquaculture degradation, with fish farms expanding by 17.63 km2/yr alongside massive agricultural drains. Bardawil (open system) experienced a threefold increase in very high rTDS zones (Sen’s Slope = +8.70 km2/yr) due solely to aquaculture infrastructure restricting marine flushing. Synthesizing these findings, the apparent reduction in extreme degradation zones is a misleading indicator of recovery, reflecting progressive homogenization. The driving mechanisms vary fundamentally by hydrological connectivity: closed systems suffer pollutant retention; partially open systems face restricted inlets; restricted-exchange systems suffer internal stagnation; and open lagoons face infrastructure fragmentation. Therefore, sustainable management requires lake-specific interventions tailored to each connectivity status, focusing on nutrient reduction, hydrological restoration, and aquaculture regulation.

nodes.name: Predicting optical turbulence from ground measurements: a machine learning approach to C2n estimation in the surface layer
nodes.venue: Environmental Effects on Light Propagation and Adaptive Systems IX
nodes.abstract: Optical turbulence describes spatio-temporal fluctuations of the atmospheric refractive index structure parameter C<sub>n</sub>² and plays a central role in determining the atmospheric distortion in applications such as free-space optical communication, or laser beam propagation. The pronounced variability on short temporal and spatial scales, however, complicates accurate characterization. Turbulence is typically assessed either with dedicated instrumentation or indirectly via meteorological standard measurements and numerical modelling. Models often exhibit insufficient accuracy, and direct measurements are frequently unavailable or geographically limited. To overcome these limitations, this work aims to develop a machine learning model that estimates optical turbulence values and provides predictions —along with vertical profiling in the surface layer— from ground-based measurements. We used a data set of approximately six years, collected at a site in Meppen, Germany. C<sub>n</sub>² was measured with a laser-scintillometer along a path of 75m and with sonic anemometers on a tower in 4m, 8m, 32m and 64m altitude. Standard meteorological observations were made at the same heights and extended by measurements of pressure and radiation. These data are used to train and test a machine learning model. The model used here is an LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) network designed to capture temporal dependencies and provide short-horizon predictions. To assess prediction accuracy, an uncertainty estimate is provided for each predicted value. First results will be presented.

nodes.name: Environmental Effects on Light Propagation and Adaptive Systems IX
Orientation-Aware Feature Flow Network for Oriented Object Detection in Remote Sensing Images
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Remote sensing oriented object detection faces the challenge of maintaining consistent rotational geometric information throughout feature representation, cross-scale propagation, and bounding-box localization. To address this issue, this paper proposes a direction–scale collaborative optimization method for oriented object detection. A frozen DINOv3 encoder is adopted as the semantic feature source to enhance target discrimination in complex backgrounds through global semantic modeling and dense feature representation. Rotation-Oriented Space-to-Depth Convolution (ROSPD) is introduced to preserve fine-grained spatial structures and local directional-response cues during downsampling. In addition, a Rotation-Aware Residual Fusion (RARF) module estimates local axial agreement between adjacent feature levels and uses it to condition residual multi-scale fusion. A ProbIoU–NWD joint loss with deterministic target-size-adaptive weighting is further constructed: it emphasizes NWD supervision for small objects and gradually returns to ProbIoU as target size increases, thereby improving localization stability under low-overlap conditions. Experiments on DIOR-R and DOTA-v1.5 demonstrate that the proposed method effectively improves the detection and localization performance of multi-scale oriented objects in complex remote sensing scenes.

nodes.name: Multipoint fiber-optic sensing via sensor fusion of speckle and polarization interrogation
nodes.venue: Electro-Optical and Infrared Systems: Technology and Applications XXIII
nodes.abstract: High-bandwidth, spatially resolved acoustic sensing is essential for applications such as structural health monitoring, critical infrastructure surveillance, and predictive maintenance. While optical fiber sensing offers significant advantages in these scenarios, existing distributed sensing technologies remain constrained by system complexity and tradeoffs between spatial resolution and interrogation bandwidth. In this work, we present a dual-modality fiber-optic sensing architecture that combines speckle dynamics and polarization interrogation within a unified sensor fusion framework. Speckle interrogation provides spatial localization of perturbations across four calibrated sensing locations along a 4m fiber, while the polarization channel reconstructs the corresponding temporal waveform. By assigning complementary sensing tasks to each modality, the proposed approach over comes the bandwidth limitations of camera-based speckle interrogation while preserving localization capability. Experimental results demonstrate broadband waveform reconstruction from 100Hz to 40kHz with a signal to-noise ratio of 35dB, together with perturbation localization at separations down to 3cm and an overall localization accuracy of approximately 97% across 1000 events. These results demonstrate the potential of multimodal interrogation as a compact and scalable approach for simultaneous localization and broadband vibration sensing.

nodes.name: Electro-Optical and Infrared Systems: Technology and Applications XXIII
Mesoscale modelling of optical turbulence and aerosol attenuation for laser satellite communications
nodes.venue: Environmental Effects on Light Propagation and Adaptive Systems IX
nodes.abstract: Ground-to-satellite laser links are susceptible to atmospheric phenomena. We present a modelling toolbox to account for atmospheric effects on operationally relevant laser satellite links with a focus on optical turbulence and aerosols. We model 𝐶<sub>n</sub>² vertical profiles and column aerosol attenuation using the mesoscale models WRF and LE, respectively, under clear-sky and cloudy conditions. To capture the variability along the path, especially relevant for optical turbulence, we use ultra-high vertical resolution (50m in the boundary layer and 100m above). The resulting 𝐶<sub>n</sub>² profiles are validated against turbulence data from an optical scintillometer and sonic anemometers at various heights at Cabauw, a turbulence test-bed in the Netherlands. Following validation, we apply the methodology for optical turbulence and aerosols to an operationally relevant maritime environment. Finally, we analyse the impact of turbulence and aerosol attenuation in ground-to-satellite vertical links by estimating optical link losses.

nodes.name: Mapping soil organic carbon with Soil Health Card observations and multisensor satellite data in Odisha, India
nodes.abstract: Abstract Soil organic carbon contributes to soil fertility and terrestrial carbon storage, making its spatial distribution important for soil assessment. We used 13,284 organic carbon measurements from India’s Soil Health Card programme and 17 optical, radar, terrain and climate covariates to map organic carbon in the upper 15 cm across Odisha, India, using a random forest on a nominal 30 m grid. A reserved 20% subset gave R² = 0.501 and a root mean square error of 0.137 percentage points. In separate five-fold assessments, R² declined from 0.468 with random folds to 0.346 when observations within 30 m were grouped, and to −0.103 with geographic-cluster folds. Coverage of nominal 90% prediction intervals declined from 90.14% under random validation to 81.96% under geographic-cluster validation. The area of applicability, defined using covariate dissimilarity, included 97.6% of mapped cropland and 68.1% of the full extent. Cropland within this domain covered 5.32 million ha and yielded upper-15-cm stock estimates of 58.83 and 77.66 Tg C under two Walkley–Black recovery assumptions. The results distinguish covariate representation from geographic predictive performance when interpreting soil organic carbon maps and stock estimates.

nodes.name: Mapping Environmental Degradation and Climate Vulnerability using GIS and Remote Sensing
nodes.venue: Kashmir Journal of Academic Research and Development
nodes.abstract: Environmental degradation and climate vulnerability pose significant threats to the stability of ecosystems, agriculture, water supply, and humans’ well-being. The use of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and remote sensing can prove beneficial in detecting spatial patterns of environmental changes, detecting signs of land degradation, and assessing regions’ vulnerability to climate threats. In this study, a geospatial framework is suggested to map environmental degradation and climate vulnerability through satellite imagery analysis, vegetation indexes, land use and land cover classification, land surface temperature, precipitation, terrain properties, and socioeconomic factors. Landsat imagery, Sentinel-2 imagery, digital elevation models, and climate gridded data will be combined in GIS to assess changes in vegetation cover, urbanization, bare lands, land surface temperature, and drought. To do that, NDVI, NDBI, LST, and precipitation anomalies will be used to derive indicators of environmental degradation. Climate Vulnerability Index (CVI) will be created using weighted overlay models with environmental exposure, sensitivity, and adaptive capacity indicators. The accuracy of classification will be measured using independent reference data sets, whereas temporal variations will be evaluated via post-classification assessment. As illustrated in the figure below, a conceptual example of the application of the framework is shown by partitioning a study site into different vulnerability zones (low, medium, high, and very high), wherein 35% of the study site has been assigned to high and very high vulnerability zones. The values are purely illustrative and are not obtained from any satellite processing. This framework can contribute to environmental monitoring, climate adaptation strategy, land management, and identification of vulnerable sites.

nodes.name: Kashmir Journal of Academic Research and Development
Machine Learning Models in Precision Agriculture for Classification of Diseases
nodes.venue: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology
nodes.abstract: The bond between machine learning models and the agriculture field is becoming stronger with each passing day. The pre-trained AlexNet, ResNet, VggNet, and GoogleNet models commonly support various tasks in the precision agriculture field, such as disease detection, nitrogen status estimation, leaf area index identification, nutrient status measuring, finding pesticide requirements, measuring growth, etc. These tasks involve a huge amount of data, such as simple cell phone images, satellite imagery data, vegetation index data, images from UAVs, and sensor data from various soil and water sensors. Analyzing and finding insight from such data is a complex task. In this article, a framework is proposed using the transfer learning method for disease classification using manual CNN model along with the pre-trained AlexNet, ResNet, and GoogleNet. The 5450-image dataset,, is considered that includes four wheat disease labels and a healthy wheat label, is used, which was constructed from publicly available datasets. The fine-tuned models are compared for the disease prediction task using the parameters such as accuracy, F1 score, recall and precision. Transfer learning ResNet50 gives promising results once fine-tuned, having the accuracy of 93% compared with other transfer learning models, which ranges from 61 % to 78%. The framework proposed can identify diseases for various crops in agriculture field.

nodes.name: MMIF: GPU-Accelerated Parallel Cryptographic Permutation Network for Secure Multimodal Medical Image Fusion in Brain Tumor Detection
nodes.abstract: Abstract The integration of complementary anatomical and functional information from various imaging modalities, such as CT, MRI, and PET, through multimodal medical image fusion has emerged as a potent technique for enhancing brain tumour diagnosis. Nevertheless, sharing and storage of fused medical images may pose serious privacy and security risks. Additionally, traditional methods for permutation diffusion encryption generally encounter sequential processing bottlenecks, making them unsuitable for real-time medical scenarios. Here we introduce a parallel cryptographic permutation network (PCPN) that blends DNA-assisted chaotic permutation and light diffusion to ensure secure and computationally efficient protection of fused medical images. At first, the fused image is divided into eight binary bit-planes. Next, a chaotic sequence generated by the logistic map is converted into DNA symbols to form distinct permutation tables for each bit-plane. The GPU-parallelised permutation allows the simultaneous scrambling of the bit planes. After that, the scrambled bit-planes are combined to form the encrypted image. Pixel-wise XOR diffusion is done by a chaotic keystream generated by a second logistic map. It not only offers avalanche characteristics and statistical randomness but also needs very low computation. By allowing independent bit-plane processing and precomputed permutation tables, the proposed system removes sequential feedback dependencies, which greatly diminishes encryption times. Experiments have indicated that our encryption scheme outperforms other schemes in cryptographic security. It accomplishes an NPCR of 99.92%, UACI of 33.48%, and entropy of 7.9992 bits/pixel. The scheme is highly resistant to differential and statistical attacks while preserving the integrity of the image. Our scheme strikes an ideal balance between protection and computational efficiency, which is a practical solution to ensure the confidentiality of multimodal medical image fusion for brain tumour diagnosis. And this method is also a very viable option for the implementation of real-time intelligent healthcare systems.

nodes.name: MADReg: Modality-aware deformation regularization for unsupervised infrared-visible image registration
nodes.venue: Measurement Science and Technology
nodes.abstract: Abstract Infrared-visible image registration establishes spatial correspondence for multisensor fusion and perception. In unsupervised deformation learning, differences in modality responses can be mistaken for geometric misalignment, causing erroneous displacement and distortion of scene geometry. Common deformation priors encourage spatial regularity, invertibility, or topology preservation, whereas determining whether a deformation is supported by the observed geometry requires additional guidance. We propose MADReg, a modality-aware deformation regularization framework that obtains complementary geometric references from reverse registration and translation-assisted registration. Bidirectional Deformation Field Consistency (BDFC) cross-utilizes the forward and backward fields and constrains the structural correspondence of the resulting warped images. Translation-Driven Deformation Regularization (TDDR) estimates auxiliary fields from translated same-modality pairs and uses their spatial displacements and amplitude and phase spectra to guide the main field. Together, these reference processes relate the estimated deformation to shared scene structures and the overall deformation patterns of auxiliary mappings, helping suppress spatial changes induced by modality responses. Within-dataset and direct cross-dataset experiments on Visnir and RoadScene demonstrate improved correspondence accuracy relative to representative methods. Ablation studies and visualizations support the complementary value of the geometric references for preserving scene structure and controlling deformation irregularity.

nodes.name: Knowledge Graph-Based DDoS Attack Detection for UAV-Assisted Space–Air–Ground Integrated Networks
nodes.venue: Drones
nodes.abstract: Distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks pose a serious threat to the availability and reliability of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted Space–Air–Ground Integrated Networks (SAGIN). In such networks, UAVs can serve as aerial access points, mobile relays, and lightweight edge nodes to provide flexible connectivity between ground users and satellite networks. However, UAV mobility, time-varying network topology, heterogeneous communication links, and constrained airborne resources lead to highly dynamic traffic patterns and cross-layer attack surfaces, making conventional DDoS detection methods difficult to directly apply. To address these challenges, this paper proposes DDoSPre-LLM, a knowledge-graph-based DDoS detection framework for UAV-assisted SAGIN. First, MulFea-LLM employs large language models to extract multidimensional attack entities and semantic relations from heterogeneous security data and constructs a SAGIN-oriented attack knowledge graph containing attack, traffic, network-resource, and UAV-related entities. Then, a graph-attention-based feature weighting mechanism dynamically evaluates the contributions of traffic volume, request frequency, access-point connections, and bandwidth utilization to different DDoS attacks. The proposed method is evaluated in a SAGIN simulation environment integrating moving UAV access/relay nodes, satellite links, and terrestrial networks. Simulation results demonstrate improved detection accuracy, F1-score, and QoS compliance, with competitive recall, AUC-ROC, and throughput preservation, compared with representative baseline methods.

nodes.name: Improved Quality‐Loss for Degradation‐State Assessment of Planetary Sun Gear via Fault Recognition
nodes.venue: Quality and Reliability Engineering International
nodes.abstract: ABSTRACT Condition‐monitoring methods commonly provide discrete fault labels, whereas maintenance assessment requires a quantitative representation of damage severity. This paper proposes a quality‐loss‐based degradation‐state assessment framework integrating cross‐speed fault recognition with severity‐weighted loss mapping for planetary sun gears to improve cross‐speed fault identification and provide severity‐aware quantitative support for degradation‐state evaluation and maintenance decision‐making. Firstly, multi‐domain features are extracted from the frequency, energy, and order domains to characterize vibration signals from the public WT‐Planetary gearbox dataset, and four machine‐learning classifiers are evaluated using a leave‐one‐speed‐out protocol to assess generalization under unseen rotational speeds. Secondly, the recognized health state is mapped to an ordinal damage index and then converted into a dimensionless relative quality‐loss index using a quadratic loss function. The proposed loss index penalizes misclassification according to the severity difference between the true and predicted states. Next, the best‐performing configuration, Boosted Trees with enhanced features, provides the most accurate and balanced cross‐speed fault recognition and severity‐weighted quality‐loss estimation among the evaluated models. Finally, increased assessment errors are observed at boundary speed conditions, particularly for Healthy and Wear states. The framework converts discrete fault‐recognition outputs into a severity‐aware quantitative indicator for degradation‐state assessment and maintenance‐oriented condition evaluation.

nodes.name: Hyperspectral Image Classification based on Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm, Deep Convolution Network and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory
nodes.venue: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology
nodes.abstract: Hyperspectral Image Classification (HIC) is very crucial for the different remote sensing applications because of its rich spectral-spatial properties. In the last decade, various Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL)-based HICs have been proposed to improve system accuracy. However, the effectiveness of HIC systems is highly challenging due to a greater number of spectral bands, complexity within each band, class imbalance, greater intricacy of DL frameworks, and poor spatial-spectral and temporal correlations across bands. This paper presents an HIC system based on a Deep Convolutional Neural Network and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (DCNN-BiLSTM) to improve the spatial, spectral, and temporal representations of the spectral bands. Furthermore, it employs an Improved Whale Optimization Algorithm (IWOA) for spectral band selection, thereby minimizing the computational intricacy of the HIC system. The IWOA-DCNN-BiLSTM provides an Overall Accuracy (OA) of 99.39%, a recall of 99.31%, a precision of 99.40%, and an F1-score of 99.35% for the Indian Pines Dataset (IPD). The proposed IWOA-based band selection scheme offers lower computational complexity and higher HIC accuracy than traditional techniques.

nodes.name: Geospatial Decision Support for Vacant-Land-Based Tertiary Hospital Siting: Pareto Enumeration of Multimodal Accessibility–Equity Scenarios in Beijing
nodes.venue: Applied Sciences
nodes.abstract: Equitable access to tertiary healthcare contributes to sustainable urban development. We develop a geospatial decision-support framework to evaluate vacant-land siting of tertiary hospitals in Beijing and its implications for potential accessibility and spatial equity. Existing work has not jointly enumerated all combinations in a finite candidate set and compared aggregate results with district-level disparities. Using data for 13,109 residential communities, 82 existing tertiary hospitals, and 23 candidate parcels, we enumerate every combination of one to five new sites. S1–S5 denote scenarios with one to five sites, respectively. We use the published multimodal accessibility model, collect route costs for candidate-site–community pairs, estimate candidate-hospital staffing from parcel area using a linear regression calibrated on existing hospitals, and assess population-weighted accessibility and the Gini coefficient. Pareto fronts identify non-dominated combinations; an equal-weight normalized ideal-point rule selects compromise solutions. The five scenarios contain 23, 253, 1771, 8855, and 33,649 combinations, with 2, 6, 8, 10, and 13 non-dominated solutions, respectively. The tied one-site compromises, S1-A at site 16 and S1-B at site 19, increase weighted accessibility by 8.88% and 3.37%, while Gini changes by +0.84% and −0.48%, respectively. S2–S5 increase weighted accessibility by 12.61–29.02% and reduce Gini by 0.01–0.85%. These are model-based scenario estimates, not implemented or empirically validated siting outcomes. The framework can inform other urban facility-location analyses when local data and accessibility models are adapted.
